ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, an ideal step-down transformer connected to a household circuit supplies power to the small light bulb L. If the primary and secondary coils are reduced by the same number of turns, with other conditions unchanged, how will the brightness of the small light bulb change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The small light bulb becomes dimmer
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the coil on the left is labeled n1 and is connected to the AC power supply symbol; the coil on the right is labeled n2 and forms a closed circuit with the small light bulb L. There is an iron core symbol between the left and right coils, indicating a transformer. The problem statement explains that this is an ideal step-down transformer connected to a household circuit, so the primary coil is connected to a constant household AC voltage, and step-down means n1>n2. Reasoning: An ideal transformer satisfies U2/U1=n2/n1. When other conditions are unchanged, the primary-side voltage U1 remains unchanged. If the primary and secondary coils are each reduced by the same number of turns Δ, then the new voltage ratio is U2'/U1=(n2-Δ)/(n1-Δ). Because n1>n2, (n2-Δ)/(n1-Δ)<n2/n1, that is, the secondary-coil output voltage U2' becomes smaller. The voltage across the bulb decreases, the power obtained decreases, and the brightness decreases.
